difficulty_reason: The lemma gives four equivalent formulations, at a prime, of the statement that a finite module is generated by k elements there: non-containment of the k-th Fitting ideal in the prime, the dimension of the fibre being at most k, generation by k elements after localising, and generation by k elements after inverting a single element outside the prime. The proof first observes, using Nakayama's lemma, that generation of the fibre by k elements spreads to a localisation at one element, which gives the equivalence of the last three conditions; then the base change behaviour of Fitting ideals reduces the comparison with the first condition to the case of a module over a field, where the statement is the elementary computation of the Fitting ideal of a vector space.
